newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on wheat, weather ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on wheat, weather ideas.

text.p: Nearly ideal soybean crop weather in South America plus a steep slide in wheat futures pressed CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"It was in the market yesterday but they're still talking about South America looking good," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybean seedings are ahead of average in Brazil plus Argentine weather remains good for the soybean and corn crops, traders said.
"There's continued bearish weather," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

"It (Jan soy) is trying to hold above $7.00 but continues testing it. It will have to stay above $7.00 or we could be in trouble," Lespinasse said. The session low for January was $6.98 which was set on the close and was below Monday's low of $6.99-1/2.
Soy was underpinned by aggressive weekly soybean crushings and slow farmer selling near the $7.00 mark in Jan.
Soybeans closed 4-1/2 to seven cents per bushel lower, with January down 4-1/2 at $6.99.

Key players included ADM Investor Services with three million bushels purchased in the March and 1.5 million in January, traders said. Refco Inc sold three million January and Griffin Trading sold three million bushels of March, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 48,000 contracts, below the 57,816 traded Monday.

In soybean options, The Chicago Corp sold 250 January $7.00 puts at 6-1/4 to 7-1/4 cents, Tenco Inc sold 200 January $7.25 calls at 2-1/8 to 2-1/2 cents and Refco Inc bought 200 January $6.75 puts at 1-3/8 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, above the 12,765 traded Monday.
